prompt:
A hockey player strikes a stationary puck of mass 0.17 kg on ice. The contact time between the stick and the puck is 12 ms. The puck leaves the stick with a horizontal speed of 24 m s^-1. Calculate:
(a) the change in momentum of the puck [1]
(b) the average force exerted by the stick on the puck [2]

mark_scheme.criterion: Calculates Delta p = mv = 0.17 * 24 = 4.08 N s (accept 4.1 N s or 4.08 kg m s^-1).
Converts contact time: 12 ms = 0.012 s and uses F = Delta p / Delta t.

hints: In part (a), the puck starts from rest, so Delta p = mv.
In part (b), convert milliseconds to seconds before dividing.
solution:
(a) Delta p = 0.17 kg * 24 m s^-1 = 4.08 kg m s^-1 (or 4.1 N s).
(b) F = Delta p / Delta t = 4.08 / 0.012 s = 340 N.
teacher_walkthrough: Part (a): Initial velocity is zero, so Delta p = mv = 0.17 * 24 = 4.08 N s.
Part (b): Convert 12 ms to 0.012 s. Apply F = Delta p / Delta t = 4.08 / 0.012 = 340 N.
